title: Why Rodrigo Paz Is Trying to Distance Himself From “MAGA’s Man in Latin America”
author: Joseph Bouchard
content:

A political operative who helped engineer far-right political victories across
Latin America is now[ jailed](https://www.lanacion.com.ar/el-
mundo/trasladaron-a-cerimedo-a-una-carcel-de-maxima-seguridad-en-bolivia-y-
sorprendio-con-un-mensaje-para-nid08092026/) in Bolivia for allegedly hiring a
hitman to murder his pregnant ex-girlfriend. He also has strong ties to
Trumpworld and played a key role as an adviser to Bolivian President Rodrigo
Paz, functioning in effect as a shadow cabinet member with more influence than
some of the government's actual ministers.

Like many others in the far-right political universe, Paz is now trying
mightily to distance himself from Fernando Cerimedo, who built his career
running bot networks and[ disinformation
operations](https://jacobin.com/2026/09/cerimedo-latin-america-far-right-
disinformation) across Latin America. Cerimedo was the strategic[
mastermind](https://www.latimes.com/world-nation/story/2026-09-13/he-was-
called-magas-man-in-latin-america-now-hes-charged-with-murder) behind a number
of far-right political victories in the region, including in[ Argentina,
Chile, Bolivia, and Colombia](https://jacobin.com/2026/09/cerimedo-latin-
america-far-right-disinformation). He has[ documented U.S. lobbying
ties](https://www.thebulwark.com/p/murder-for-hire-plot-rocking-maga-trump-
brad-parscale-bolivia-fernando-cerimedo) running through former Trump campaign
manager [Brad Parscale](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/israel-brad-parscale-
ai-chatbots-gaza) and Miami consultant[ Damian
Merlo](https://efile.fara.gov/docs/6898-Exhibit-AB-20230929-9.pdf). In
Bolivia, he was Paz's chief adviser for the 2025 campaign that ended nearly
two decades of socialist rule by former President Evo Morales' MAS party.

Soon after taking office, Paz cut taxes for the ultra-rich, invited American
investment and IMF financing, looked to privatize indigenous lands in an
indigenous-majority country, and invited the U.S. Southern Command and Drug
Enforcement Administration back into the country. He also began prosecuting
MAS and left-wing figures, jailing former President Luis Arce and prominent
union leaders, and went after former President Evo Morales. Cerimedo had spent
months pushing for these policies, both publicly and privately, and used his
social media accounts to wage war on what he called "dirty leftists."

post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fa73d3a41-876d-4bc8-b125-7424b63bb1de_970x1176.png)Screenshot
of a tweet by Secretary of State Marco Rubio highlighting his meeting with
Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz.

According to [Vice President Edman
Lara](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=962609726852494), Cerimedo kept an
office near the president's own workspace in the Palacio Quemado, wrote
speeches, and controlled access to Paz himself. He was present at the "Shield
of the Americas" summit at Mar-a-Lago, the Trump administration's regional
security initiative, [sitting
across](https://www.wsws.org/en/articles/2026/09/01/vyag-s01.html) from
Secretary of State Marco Rubio and alongside Paz and his chief of staff
Fernando Aramayo.

"During press conferences, [Cerimedo] would direct the media, and even us and
the cabinet members, as if he was orchestrating the whole thing," one staffer
in the Bolivian Ministry of Foreign Affairs told Drop Site, who requested
their name be withheld over fears of reprisal.

Bolivian Plurinational Deputy Claudia Herbas told Drop Site that Bolivia's
President Rodrigo Paz "lied to the public" about his relationship with
Cerimedo.

"[He] said there was no relationship, when we had direct concrete evidence to
the contrary. There is clearly a cover up of the facts, and denial of reality
by this government," said Herbas.

Cerimedo was arrested August 18, 2026 at the Santa Cruz airport, allegedly
trying to flee to Buenos Aires, and is accused of planning the killing of his
Bolivian girlfriend, Nadia Beller, who survived being shot three times by
assassins posing as app-based delivery drivers. Prosecutors allege that
Cerimedo contracted hitmen to kill Beller over fears she would expose his
alleged criminal actions. Since the shooting, Beller has appeared from her
hospital bed in media outlets throughout Latin America, sharing intimate
details of her former partner's work.

Since Cerimedo's arrest Paz has tried to distance himself, publishing a
crudely edited, nearly five-minute video denying claims that Cerimedo acted in
an official capacity. During his transfer to the high-security Chonchocoro
prison, Cerimedo delivered a message to Paz, telling a local outlet: "May he
forgive me for not heeding his advice."

One former advisor to Paz, who left his government post over policy
disagreements, alleged that there is a government effort to cover up Cermido's
role in the government.

"It is clear that nobody involved is being honest about what transpired," said
the advisor, who requested anonymity to avoid retaliation.

A [leaked recording](https://brujuladigital.net/politica/2026/09/13/cerimedo-
participaba-en-grupos-de-whastapp-con-ministros-y-les-daba-ordenes-66310) of a
minister-level Bolivian official describing Cerimedo as someone who "gave
orders to ministers" has undercut Paz's own public denials of closeness to
him. Since the arrest, Cerimedo's business partner Javier Negre has also moved
to sever ties, [saying](https://www.clarin.com/politica/fernando-cerimedo-
vendio-50-derecha-diario-detenido-bolivia_0_NQwxYeC30X.html) Cerimedo agreed
to sell his 50% stake in their jointly owned right-wing outlet and Breitbart
copycat, La Derecha Diario.

Cerimedo's alleged criminal behavior extended well beyond Bolivia. Marlon
Ochoa, ousted from his post on Honduras's National Electoral Council after
objecting to certification of the 2025 vote, told Drop Site that Cerimedo, as
"[MAGA's man in Latin America](https://www.economist.com/the-
americas/2025/12/09/magas-man-in-latam)," was the intermediary between Nasry
Asfura's right-wing National Party campaign and Trumpworld.

Ochoa's complaint, filed with Attorney General Johel Zelaya on December 23,
2025, alleges Cerimedo's operation stuffed ballot boxes for Asfura, discarded
votes for other candidates, secured the alignment of the Armed Forces behind
the result, and pressured election authorities to certify a winner without a
full recount. He has since
[posted](https://x.com/MarlonOchoaHN/status/2092650782550081773) a recording
of Cerimedo describing election fraud.

In the recording, a voice Ochoa identifies as Cerimedo's says: "The votes
where more nationalist votes are coming from, if there were votes for anyone
else, they are gone, they are fixed. We will celebrate once the counting is
over."

"The elections of November 30, 2025 were marked by open external
interference," Ochoa told Drop Site. "Cerimedo is an international criminal,
an electoral filibuster in Latin America, sheltered under the mantle of
impunity of Donald Trump... he has the luxury of sailing like a pirate in our
countries, but since there is no perfect crime, he is already imprisoned in
Bolivia," he added.

Ochoa has called into question the integrity of the 2025 election, alleging
that the election authority declared a winner without counting all ballots or
processing challenges, and that Congress then impeached and expelled him from
the council for exposing it. He said he has received death threats he
attributes to allies of Cerimedo.

Julian Macias Tovar, a Madrid-based data analyst who has spent years mapping
bot networks and disinformation campaigns across Latin America and Spain, told
Drop Site that Cerimedo's operation was never a one-off.

"There's a big ecosystem, international and regional, of figures and networks
of hate and disinformation," he said, while dismissing much of Cerimedo's
personal mythology as invention. "These are all charlatans. They sell lies,
like that Cerimedo worked in the White House, and they use bots, social media
to amplify narratives, lies, and hate to sell these candidates."

Bolivian lawmaker Claudia Herbas emphasized that Cerimedo's reach went beyond
Bolivia.

"This is about a global criminal network. I have sent two petitions [to the
government] so that they can explain this to the Bolivian people," Herbas told
Drop Site.

The Chilean Chamber of Deputies
[voted](https://www.latinnews.com/component/k2/item/111334.html?archive=3&Itemid=6&cat_id=840001:chile-
congress-approves-commission-to-investigate-cerimedo-links) September 2 to
establish a special investigative commission to probe Cerimedo's political
activities, and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has
[suggested](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=1494002295865190) that the
Mexican Congress look into Cerimedo's operations as well.

"They will not stop with Cerimedo, this continues without him; digital tech,
surveillance, and social media will still be there," said Macias Tovar.

A second source close to Cerimedo who also requested anonymity for their
safety added, "Cerimedo is entirely replaceable, and the right won't let one
legal case get in the way of their gaining power."

Luis Alberto Echazu, a former minister and cabinet official under Evo Morales,
told Drop Site that Paz's work with advisors linked to foreign-influence
operations rises to the level of treason.

"The rulers who, like Rodrigo Paz, have handed over state political decisions
to this kind of foreign agent disguised as advisors must be put on trial for
treason against the homeland," said Echazu.

Bolivian lawmaker Herbas, for her part, insists that justice must be carried
out for the attempted murder of Beller and the alleged corruption by the Paz
government.

"The Cerimedo issue in our country has uncovered the mountains of corruption
we're experiencing under Rodrigo Paz's government. We need to know even more,
and we need the Prosecutor's Office and the Judiciary to truly act with
objectivity, with transparency, and we want to know what has happened,
especially regarding illicit enrichment," Herbas told Drop Site.

"This is about corruption of the president, his government, and his friends."
